## Overview

> **Writing the code was the easy part. Validating it, maintaining it, and earning the community's trust to become a standard is the ongoing work this proposal supports.**

`OptSurvCutR` was not yet on CRAN when we first applied; it is now (v0.11.1). This grant would pay for what comes next. First, a simulation study to test whether the stability grades mean what we say they mean. Second, an update to the bioRxiv preprint [@yau2025preprint] so we can submit to *BMC Bioinformatics*. Third, a simple script for researchers who are not R specialists, delivered while the `rOpenSci` review finishes. The plan runs over six months (@sec-timeline).

### Minimum Viable Product

The smallest complete deliverable is the simulation study. The manuscript is explicit about why this matters. It states that bootstrap resampling does not establish that a threshold will be recovered in an independent population, that this relationship has not been evaluated, and that the tier boundaries of 30% and 60% are "pragmatic conventions rather than calibrated thresholds." The simulation study is designed to test exactly that.

### Architecture

Both deliverables sit on top of the existing package: the simulation study is a self-contained Quarto document that tests its outputs against known ground truth, and the script wraps `find_cutpoint_number()`, `find_cutpoint()` and `validate_cutpoint()` without changing the statistical engines.

### Assumptions

- The simulation finishes on time. If the tiers turn out not to calibrate, we will report that as a finding.
- The target user for the script can run an R script but does not want to learn the full function-level API; if not, that milestone is re-scoped toward documentation.
- `rOpenSci` review continues on a compatible timeline; if it stalls, we report progress rather than completion.

### External dependencies

`survival`, `survminer`, `rgenoud`, `Rcpp`, `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `cli`, `tidyr`, `rlang`, `foreach`, `doParallel` and `doRNG` (the package's Imports at v0.11.1). No new dependencies are anticipated.
